item.title: Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
item.description: Asian shares saw significant gains as Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang made a return that relieved market fears. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose by 4.6%, while Japan's Nikkei gained 4.5% after a local holiday. This movement followed a 31.5% surge in Nvidia shares, revealing optimism in the beleaguered AI sector. United States Treasury yields climbed alongside the dollar, signaling increased confidence in Fed tightening measures.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Asian shares leapt on Tuesday following a spectacular Wall Street surge as Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO sparked a relief rally in the battered AI trade, while Federal Reserve tightening bets lifted Treasury yields and the dollar.MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6%, bouncing back from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks.Japan's Nikkei added 4.5% as traders returned from a local holiday. South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5%, while Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1%.Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout.Shares of Nvidia surged 31.5% on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in value to the company.Companies across the AI industry also rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100, which is concentrated in megacap tech companies, jumping more than 6%. The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins, despite lingering concerns about slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth, said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.There are other risks for the market as well, such as uncertainty over US interest rate policy, with investors set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data ahead of the Fed's final meeting of 2026, he added.S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2% early on Tuesday. The cash S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indexes surged 4.7% and 6.5%, respectively.AI REBOUND LIFTS FED TIGHTENING BETSThe sharp AI rebound has also eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening and lifting front-end Treasury yields and the dollar.Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the Fed's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89% odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersized 50-basis-point increase in around 5%.The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose for a second day and was last at 4.94%, and the yield on the 2-year note rose to 4.69%. The dollar, meanwhile, hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro.In commodities, oil prices fell more than 3% to near a three-month low on rising supplies from the Middle East, which offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling down 3.5% at $89.37 a barrel on Monday.Bullion recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot gold last up 0.7% at $3,657.97 per ounce as investors bought the dip.

item.title: Anthropic options draw brisk trading interest after market debut
item.description: About 160,000 Anthropic options contracts traded in the first hour, putting the AI company among the market’s most active names. Volume was on pace to exceed 600,000 contracts for the session.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Options on Anthropic shares attracted heavy trading on Monday, giving investors a new way to hedge or speculate on the artificial intelligence company just days after its stock market debut, Reuters reported.About 160,000 contracts changed hands during the first hour, placing Anthropic among the 25 most actively traded names in the options market, according to analytics firm Mercury Alerts. Volume reached roughly 270,000 contracts by noon ET.Options provide a relatively low-cost way to gain exposure to a stock and can be used either to manage risk or bet on future price movements.Also Read | Nvidia shares surge 33% as Jensen Huang is reinstated as CEO“Early trading in Anthropic options was heavy but balanced: calls and puts traded one for one, and buyers and sellers were close to even,” Mercury Alerts founder Harmeet Goindi told Reuters, adding that activity showed no clear directional bias.Anthropic’s options volume was on course to reach about 550,000 contracts by the end of the session, Mercury Alerts said. While substantial, that would remain well below the record 1.8 million contracts traded when options on SpaceX debuted in June.“We’re not seeing anything close to the sort of speculation in far upside strikes that we saw in the early days of SpaceX,” Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.For live updates on US Markets, click hereSosnick suggested that the difference could reflect the absence of what he called the “Musk factor,” referring to the investor enthusiasm often associated with SpaceX Chief Executive Elon Musk.Options pricing indicated that traders expected sharp swings in Anthropic shares.“The options are pricing moves of about 6% a day,” Goindi said.Anthropic shares fell 1.5% to $87.55, bucking a strong rebound in other AI-linked stocks after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
